basics.name: Grace Hopper
basics.label: Distinguished Engineer, Compiler Systems & Naval Computation
basics.summary: Compiler engineer and systems architect with twenty years across naval computation, commercial data processing, and standards work. Built the first practical English-language compiler, chaired the committee that turned it into a portable business language, and spent the following decade proving out machine-independent programming across eleven installations, four vendors, and three generations of hardware that shared almost nothing but arithmetic.

work.summary: Owned the compiler toolchain and its conformance suite across four hardware generations.
highlights: Shipped a machine-independent code generator retargeted to four architectures
Cut full-suite conformance runtime from 14 hours to 38 minutes
Chaired the cross-vendor standards working group through two revisions
Grew the toolchain team from 4 to 17 without lowering the review bar

work.summary: Led the group that turned an internal English-language compiler into a supported product.
highlights: Designed the intermediate representation still in use across the product line
Reduced customer-reported miscompiles by 71% over six quarters
Wrote the portability guide adopted by eleven customer installations

work.summary: Built the linking loader and the symbolic debugger for the commercial line.
highlights: Implemented the first symbolic subroutine library with automatic relocation
Halved link times by interning symbol names at assembly time
Introduced regression baselines that caught three shipping-blocker defects

work.summary: Programmed sequence-controlled calculators for ballistics and numerical analysis.
highlights: Authored the operating manual used by every subsequent operator cohort
Traced and documented the first recorded hardware-induced computation fault
Standardized tape formats across three concurrent research programs

work.summary: Taught numerical methods and built the department's first computing curriculum.
highlights: Designed a numerical-methods sequence still taught fifteen years later
Supervised 22 undergraduate theses in applied mathematics
Secured the department's first mechanical calculator budget line

work.summary: Ran the computation queue for ballistics tables under wartime deadlines.
highlights: Scheduled and verified 400+ table computations with zero published errata
Cross-trained six operators to eliminate the single-operator bottleneck
Built the checksum procedure adopted by two partner laboratories

work.summary: Computed and verified interpolation tables for the applied mathematics faculty.
highlights: Produced the interpolation tables cited in four subsequent publications
Devised a differencing check that caught transcription errors before publication
Maintained the group's reference library of numerical procedures

work.summary: Taught undergraduate algebra while completing doctoral work in mathematics.
highlights: Led six sections of undergraduate algebra across four semesters
Wrote the problem sets retained by the department for a decade
Completed doctoral research on irreducibility criteria
